1	// Command git-remote-entire is the git remote helper for entire:// URLs.
2	//
3	// Git resolves `git clone entire://host/project/repo` by exec'ing a binary
4	// named git-remote-entire on PATH, handing it the remote-helper protocol on
5	// stdin and reading responses from stdout. This is a small, dedicated
6	// binary (no cobra command tree) that shares the protocol, transport, and
7	// auth packages with the main entire CLI.
8	//
9	// IMPORTANT: nothing here may write to stdout except the helper protocol
10	// itself — git parses stdout as a strict pkt-line stream, so a stray banner
11	// or log line corrupts the transfer. Diagnostics go to stderr (and the
12	// ENTIRE_DEBUG-gated debuglog).
13	//
14	// Authentication resolves the login context for the target cluster from the
15	// shared contexts.json: the cluster's cores come from the cluster_cores.json
16	// cache (or a live /.well-known fetch on miss), then the account is selected
17	// from local contexts. It then mints a jurisdiction access token by
18	// exchanging that context's login JWT (or ENTIRE_TOKEN in CI).
19	package main
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"errors"
24		"fmt"
25		"io"

27		"net/url"

37		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo"
38		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery"
39		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/httpclient"
40		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/httputil"
41		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/userdirs"
42		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper"
43		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/debuglog"
44		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/githelper"
45		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/httpdebug"
46		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/replicas"
47		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/remotehelper/transport"
48	)

50	func main() {
51		os.Exit(run(os.Args))
52	}
53	
54	func run(args []string) int {
55		// --version / --help only activate as the sole argument (so os.Args has
56		// length 2). Git always invokes the helper as
57		// `git-remote-entire <remote-name> <url>` (os.Args length 3), so these can
58		// never collide with a real remote-helper invocation.
59		if len(args) == 2 {
60			if text, ok := infoFlagText(args[1], loadedVersion()); ok {
61				fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, text)
62				return 0
63			}
64		}
65	
66		if len(args) < 3 {
67			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "usage: %s <remote-name> <url>\n", remotehelper.BinaryName)
68			return 128
69		}
70	
71		// Build info drives the identifier the helper advertises upstream.
72		// One string covers both surfaces:
73		//   - githelper.Agent rides in the git protocol pkt-line agent=
74		//     capability appended to upload-pack / receive-pack / v2 requests.
75		//   - httpUserAgent rides in the HTTP User-Agent header on every
76		//     outbound request so server access logs can attribute traffic.
77		// Using the same value keeps the two log surfaces correlatable.
78		versioninfo.Load()
79		helperAgent := remotehelper.BinaryName + "/" + versioninfo.Version
80		githelper.Agent = helperAgent
81		httpUserAgent := helperAgent
82	
83		rawURL := args[2]
84		parsedURL, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
85		switch {
86		case err != nil:
87			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: invalid URL %q: %v\n", rawURL, err)
88			return 128
89		case parsedURL.Scheme != "entire":
90			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: unsupported URL scheme %q (expected 'entire')\n", parsedURL.Scheme)
91			return 128
92		case parsedURL.Host == "":
93			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: missing host in URL %q\n", rawURL)
94			return 128
95		}
96	
97		ctx, stop := installSignals()
98		defer stop()
99	
100		skipTLS := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY") == "true"
101	
102		nodeCfg := replicas.Resolve(parsedURL)
103	
104		// This client drives the auth path only: cluster /.well-known discovery
105		// and the token exchange. Both talk to a single control-plane host with no
106		// failover to fall back on, so they get the patient discovery dial budget
107		// (DiscoveryDialTimeout, i.e. DefaultDiscoveryDialTimeout unless
108		// ENTIRE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS overrides it) rather than the short failover
109		// one — a slow cold connect here would otherwise fail the whole clone/fetch.
110		httpClient := &http.Client{
111			Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
112			Transport: &httpclient.UserAgentTransport{
113				Next: &httpdebug.TimingRoundTripper{
114					Next:  httpclient.NewDiscoveryTransport(skipTLS),
115					Label: "auth",
116				},
117				UA: httpUserAgent,
118			},
119		}
120	
121		creds, err := resolveCreds(ctx, parsedURL, skipTLS, httpClient)
122		if err != nil {
123			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "fatal: %v\n", err)
124			return 128
125		}
126	
127		setAuth := func(req *http.Request) error {
128			// Refuse to attach credentials to a request we can't classify as a
129			// known git smart-HTTP endpoint. The jurisdiction token doesn't
130			// need the action, but sending a bearer to an unexpected endpoint
131			// is never right.
132			action := gitActionFromRequest(req)
133			if action == "" {
134				return fmt.Errorf("refusing to attach credentials: %s %s is not a recognised git smart-HTTP endpoint", req.Method, req.URL.Path)
135			}
136			start := time.Now()
137			token, err := creds.Token(req.Context())
138			if err != nil {
139				return fmt.Errorf("git credential exchange: %w", err)
140			}
141			debuglog.Printf("timing: token-acquire action=%s dur_ms=%d (keychain + login refresh + exchange; ~0 when memoized)", action, time.Since(start).Milliseconds())
142			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
143			return nil
144		}
145	
146		var onNodeFailed func(string)
147		if nodeCfg.Caching() {
148			onNodeFailed = func(string) { replicas.Invalidate(nodeCfg.ClusterHost, nodeCfg.RepoPath) }
149		}
150	
151		proxy := transport.New(transport.Config{
152			Nodes:   nodeCfg,
153			Path:    parsedURL.Path,
154			SkipTLS: skipTLS,
155			SetAuth: setAuth,
156			// A 401 means the data plane rejected the credential itself (e.g.
157			// signing-key rotation invalidated a persisted jurisdiction token) —
158			// drop it so the next invocation re-mints instead of failing until
159			// the token's recorded expiry. The env-token source persists
160			// nothing; it drops only its in-process memo.
161			OnUnauthorized: creds.Invalidate,
162			OnNodeFailed:   onNodeFailed,
163			UserAgent:      httpUserAgent,
164		})
165	
166		protocolVersion := resolveProtocolVersion()
167		debuglog.Printf("git protocol.version=%d (v2 advertises stateless-connect + push; v0/v1 advertises connect)", protocolVersion)
168	
169		helperStart := time.Now()
170		if err := githelper.Run(ctx, proxy, protocolVersion, os.Stdin, os.Stdout); err != nil {
171			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, fatalMessage(err, parsedURL))
172			return 128
173		}
174		debuglog.Printf("timing: helper-session dur_ms=%d", time.Since(helperStart).Milliseconds())
175		return 0
176	}
177	
178	// wrongClusterRe extracts the host that actually serves the repo from the
179	// data plane's `invalid_target` error_description (RFC 8693). The data plane
180	// emits this when the audience host doesn't host the repo but a sibling
181	// cluster does, naming the correct host so we can point the user at it. The
182	// phrasing is "… it lives on \"<host>\" …"; anchoring on "lives on" keeps the
183	// match tied to this specific, actionable case rather than other
184	// invalid_target variants (e.g. a suspended mirror).
185	var wrongClusterRe = regexp.MustCompile(`lives on "([^"]+)"`)
186	
187	// fatalMessage renders the stderr "fatal: …" line for a transfer error. When
188	// the failure is the data plane reporting that the repo lives on a different
189	// cluster, it special-cases the raw OAuth chain into an actionable message
190	// naming the correct host (and the corrected entire:// URL). Everything else
191	// falls back to the verbatim error.
192	func fatalMessage(err error, parsedURL *url.URL) string {
193		var oe *httputil.OAuthError
194		if errors.As(err, &oe) && oe.Code == "invalid_target" {
195			if m := wrongClusterRe.FindStringSubmatch(oe.Description); m != nil {
196				host := m[1]
197				// Copy the URL the user typed and swap only the host, so any
198				// escaped path (RawPath) or query stays byte-identical to what
199				// they originally ran.
200				correctedURL := *parsedURL
201				correctedURL.Scheme = "entire"
202				correctedURL.Host = host
203				correctedURL.User = nil
204				corrected := correctedURL.String()
205				return fmt.Sprintf("fatal: this repository is not hosted on %s; it lives on %s.\n"+
206					"Re-run against the correct host, e.g.:\n\n    git clone %s\n",
207					parsedURL.Host, host, corrected)
208			}
209		}
210		return fmt.Sprintf("fatal: %v\n", err)
211	}
212	
213	// loadedVersion populates the build info and returns the resolved version.
214	func loadedVersion() string {
215		versioninfo.Load()
216		return versioninfo.Version
217	}
218	
219	// infoFlagText renders the output for the standalone --version / --help flags,
220	// returning false for anything else. Kept pure (version passed in, no globals)
221	// so it's unit-testable.
222	func infoFlagText(flag, version string) (string, bool) {
223		switch flag {
224		case "--version":
225			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\nGo version: %s\nOS/Arch: %s/%s\n",
226				remotehelper.BinaryName, version, runtime.Version(), runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH), true
227		case "--help":
228			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\n\n"+
229				"This is a helper which Git calls when encountering entire://... URLs.  "+
230				"For more information see https://github.com/entireio/cli.\n",
231				remotehelper.BinaryName, version), true
232		}
233		return "", false
234	}
235	
236	// resolveProtocolVersion reads the effective protocol.version from
237	// the GIT_PROTOCOL environment variable. The value is a colon-
238	// separated list of key=value pairs (e.g. "version=2"). We accept
239	// 0, 1, or 2; any other value emits a stderr warning and falls
240	// back to 2 — upstream Git's default since 2.26.
241	func resolveProtocolVersion() int {
242		return parseProtocolVersion(os.Getenv("GIT_PROTOCOL"), os.Stderr)
243	}
244	
245	func parseProtocolVersion(raw string, warn io.Writer) int {
246		const defaultVersion = 2
247		for kv := range strings.SplitSeq(raw, ":") {
248			k, v, ok := strings.Cut(kv, "=")
249			if !ok || k != "version" {
250				continue
251			}
252			switch v {
253			case "0":
254				return 0
255			case "1":
256				return 1
257			case "2":
258				return 2
259			}
260			fmt.Fprintf(warn, "git-remote-entire: ignoring unrecognised protocol.version=%q; defaulting to %d\n", v, defaultVersion)
261			return defaultVersion
262		}
263		return defaultVersion
264	}
265	
266	// resolveCreds builds the git-credential source. Both paths mint a
267	// jurisdiction access token; they differ in what session credential seeds
268	// the exchange and where the token is cached:
269	//
270	//   - ENTIRE_TOKEN set: use the env JWT verbatim as the session credential,
271	//     exchanging it at the core derived from its aud claim. Skips
272	//     contexts.json and the keyring entirely — the CI / workload path,
273	//     memoized in-process only. A non-URL aud is a hard error, never a
274	//     silent fallback to context resolution.
275	//   - otherwise: resolve the login context for this cluster from contexts.json
276	//     and mint a keychain-persisted jurisdiction access token from its
277	//     stored login JWT.
278	func resolveCreds(ctx context.Context, parsedURL *url.URL, skipTLS bool, httpClient *http.Client) (*jurisdictionTokenSource, error) {
279		// Presence of ENTIRE_TOKEN is the signal: if it's set at all (LookupEnv,
280		// not Getenv, so we can tell set-empty from unset), we commit to the
281		// env-token path and any failure to use it is fatal — never a silent
282		// fallback to context auth, which would mask a misconfigured CI runner.
283		// Read and trim once here, the only place we touch it, so every downstream
284		// consumer (aud derivation and the exchanged subject_token) sees the
285		// cleaned value; a trailing newline from $(cat token) is common. An empty
286		// or whitespace-only value fails closed.
287		if raw, ok := os.LookupEnv(auth.EnvTokenVar); ok {
288			envToken := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
289			if envToken == "" {
290				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is set but blank", auth.EnvTokenVar)
291			}
292			return resolveEnvTokenCreds(ctx, envToken, parsedURL.Host, userdirs.Cache(), httpClient)
293		}
294	
295		// Resolve which login context authenticates this cluster: the cluster's
296		// login servers are taken from the cluster_cores.json cache (or a live
297		// /.well-known fetch on miss/expiry), then the account is selected from
298		// local contexts — active context if eligible, else the sole eligible
299		// one, else an explicit-choice error.
300		cfgDir := userdirs.Config()
301		clusterAuth, err := clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterAuth(ctx, cfgDir, userdirs.Cache(), parsedURL.Host, httpClient, debuglog.Printf)
302		if err != nil {
303			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ResolveClusterAuth already returns a user-facing error; preserved verbatim for the "fatal: <msg>" surface
304		}
305		clusterCtx := clusterAuth.Context
306	
307		// The login-JWT provider transparently refreshes an expired login JWT
308		// from the stored refresh token (serialised across processes, rotated
309		// tokens persisted) before the jurisdiction-token exchange consumes it.
310		loginProvider, err := auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider(clusterCtx, httpClient.Transport, skipTLS)
311		if err != nil {
312			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // NewRefreshingLoginProvider already returns a user-facing error
313		}
314	
315		// One keychain-persisted jurisdiction access token authenticates every
316		// repo (authorized live at the data plane) — there is no repo-scoped
317		// fallback on this path. The cluster must advertise its jurisdiction
318		// audience.
319		audience := clusterAuth.JurisdictionAudience
320		if audience == "" {
321			return nil, missingJurisdictionAudienceErr(parsedURL.Host)
322		}
323		debuglog.Printf("auth: jurisdiction access token (aud=%s, core=%s)", audience, clusterCtx.CoreURL)
324		return newJurisdictionTokenSource(clusterCtx.CoreURL, audience, clusterAuth.JurisdictionCoreURL, clusterCtx.Handle, loginProvider, httpClient), nil
325	}
326	
327	// resolveEnvTokenCreds builds the jurisdiction-token source for the
328	// ENTIRE_TOKEN path. Split out of resolveCreds with explicit
329	// clusterHost/cacheDir params (no os.Getenv / userdirs.Cache globals) so the
330	// trust gate below is unit-testable against a fake well-known server.
331	//
332	// The exchange runs at the env token's own core with the cluster's advertised
333	// jurisdiction audience. No home/cross-jurisdiction routing is needed: the
334	// trust gate guarantees that core fronts the target cluster, so it owns the
335	// cluster's jurisdiction audience.
336	//
337	// SECURITY: coreURL is derived from the env token's *unverified* aud claim, and
338	// it becomes the host the token is POSTed to as a subject_token during
339	// exchange. Before trusting it, we confirm the core is one the target cluster
340	// actually advertises — anchored to the clone URL's host the user typed (TLS to
341	// its /.well-known/entire-cluster.json), not to the token's own claims. Without
342	// this gate a forged aud could redirect the token to an attacker-chosen host.
343	//
344	// The gate is only as strong as that TLS verification: with
345	// ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true (a local-dev escape hatch) the well-known fetch
346	// is no longer authenticated, so a MITM could advertise an attacker host as a
347	// trusted core. Do not combine ENTIRE_TOKEN with ENTIRE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY in
348	// CI / workload environments.
349	func resolveEnvTokenCreds(ctx context.Context, envToken, clusterHost, cacheDir string, httpClient *http.Client) (*jurisdictionTokenSource, error) {
350		coreURL, err := auth.CoreURLFromEnvToken(envToken)
351		if err != nil {
352			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // CoreURLFromEnvToken already returns a user-facing, ENTIRE_TOKEN-prefixed error
353		}
354		cluster, err := clusterdiscovery.ResolveClusterCores(ctx, cacheDir, clusterHost, httpClient, debuglog.Printf)
355		if err != nil {
356			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ResolveClusterCores returns a user-facing discovery error
357		}
358		if !coreTrusted(coreURL, cluster.CoreURLs) {
359			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s aud %q is not a trusted login server for cluster %s (advertised: %s); the token belongs to a different cluster",
360				auth.EnvTokenVar, coreURL, clusterHost, strings.Join(cluster.CoreURLs, ", "))
361		}
362		if cluster.JurisdictionAudience == "" {
363			return nil, missingJurisdictionAudienceErr(clusterHost)
364		}
365		hint := crossJurisdictionHint(coreURL, clusterHost, cluster.JurisdictionCoreURL)
366		if hint != "" {
367			debuglog.Printf("auth: %s core %s differs from cluster %s's jurisdiction core %s; the exchange will likely be refused", auth.EnvTokenVar, coreURL, clusterHost, cluster.JurisdictionCoreURL)
368		}
369		debuglog.Printf("auth: %s jurisdiction access token (aud=%s, core=%s)", auth.EnvTokenVar, cluster.JurisdictionAudience, coreURL)
370		return newEnvJurisdictionTokenSource(coreURL, cluster.JurisdictionAudience, envToken, hint, httpClient), nil
371	}
372	
373	// crossJurisdictionHint pre-computes the actionable message for the one
374	// misconfiguration the trust gate can't catch: an ENTIRE_TOKEN minted at a
375	// core of a different jurisdiction than the cluster's. Clusters advertise
376	// every jurisdiction's cores as trusted login servers, so such a token
377	// passes the gate — but the exchange is doomed, because only the cluster's
378	// own jurisdiction core mints for its audience, and the core-side refusal
379	// is an opaque invalid_target. Returned as a suffix for that eventual
380	// exchange error rather than a hard pre-flight failure: clusters may
381	// advertise several same-jurisdiction core URLs, so inequality here is a
382	// strong hint, not proof.
383	func crossJurisdictionHint(coreURL, clusterHost, jurisdictionCoreURL string) string {
384		if jurisdictionCoreURL == "" {
385			return ""
386		}
387		if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimRight(coreURL, "/"), strings.TrimRight(jurisdictionCoreURL, "/")) {
388			return ""
389		}
390		return fmt.Sprintf("\n%s was minted at %s, but cluster %s's jurisdiction core is %s — point your CI auth url at %s",
391			auth.EnvTokenVar, coreURL, clusterHost, jurisdictionCoreURL, jurisdictionCoreURL)
392	}
393	
394	// missingJurisdictionAudienceErr names the one condition both auth paths
395	// refuse on: a cluster that predates jurisdiction-token git auth.
396	func missingJurisdictionAudienceErr(clusterHost string) error {
397		return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s advertises no jurisdiction_audience at %s; its entire-server predates jurisdiction-token git auth", clusterHost, clusterdiscovery.Path)
398	}
399	
400	// coreTrusted reports whether coreURL is in the cluster's advertised core
401	// set, comparing on trailing-slash-insensitive equality to match how core
402	// URLs are compared elsewhere (contexts.ContextsForIssuer, auth.sameIssuer).
403	func coreTrusted(coreURL string, trusted []string) bool {
404		want := strings.TrimRight(coreURL, "/")
405		for _, t := range trusted {
406			if strings.TrimRight(t, "/") == want {
407				return true
408			}
409		}
410		return false
411	}
412	
413	// gitActionFromRequest classifies a smart-HTTP request as "pull" or "push".
414	// The jurisdiction token doesn't vary by action, but the classification
415	// still gates which endpoints may carry credentials (and labels the timing
416	// logs). Returns "" when the endpoint isn't a recognised git smart-HTTP
417	// route.
418	func gitActionFromRequest(req *http.Request) string {
419		path := req.URL.Path
420		switch req.Method {
421		case http.MethodPost:
422			switch {
423			case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/git-receive-pack"):
424				return "push"
425			case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/git-upload-pack"):
426				return "pull"

func missingClusterHostMessage(parsedURL *url.URL, rawURL string) string {

## The comments

Two automated reviewers ran — **Cursor Bugbot** and **GitHub Copilot** — and both landed on the **same single, valid issue** (no human comments yet):

> `missingClusterHostMessage` suggested `entire repo clone` for *any* forge id in the host slot, without checking that owner **and** repo were present. So `entire://gh` produced the hint `entire repo clone /gh`, and `entire://gh/owner` produced `/gh/owner` — refs that `parseMirrorCloneRef` (`^/?gh/<owner>/<repo>$`) rejects immediately. Worse, the *empty-host* branch already fell back correctly, so `entire://gh/owner` and `entire:///gh/owner` — the same mistake — behaved inconsistently.

I verified this against `repo_clone.go:24` (`mirrorCloneRefRe`): the ref must be a complete `gh/<owner>/<repo>` triple. Anything shorter (`entire://gh`, `.../owner`), longer (extra segments), or non-forge falls back to the plain `missing host` error. This also fixes the inconsistency between the two URL shapes.
- Collapsing the two branches let me inline the now-single-use `clusterHostHint`.
